content:
Alex (Sales): Hey team — Sara's POC next week. They need guidance on reserved GPUs + autoscale. Customer target: 1.2k peak concurrent sessions, avg request ~350 tokens, 95th latency target < 250ms. Any immediate blockers from infra or security?
Mira (SE): Thanks Alex. Quick checks: which model are they testing? that affects GPU footprint. Also need their QPS distribution (spiky vs steady).
Sara (Customer): We're testing a transformer-medium variant (redwood/open-med-1.2b), mixed chat and embeddings. Traffic is spiky: bursts up to 2 minutes every ~10 mins, baseline ~200 concurrent.
Zach (Infra Eng): Got it. For that model and burst pattern, suggested reserved pool = 4x A100-equivalents for steady+headroom, plus autoscale to 8 for burst headroom. Min pool 3 for baseline safety. Autoscale policy: scale by GPU increment when queue depth > 40 for >30s.
Mira (SE): Agreed. Also recommend enabling KV prefix caching and prefilling during preheat to cut token compute. Preheat plan: run warmup traffic sim that hits top-10 prompts for 15m before go-live. That reduces cold-start tail by ~60%.
Alex (Sales): Can you estimate cost delta if we move from 4 reserved -> 8 reserved vs reserved+burst credits? Customer cares about predictable monthly commit.
Zach (Infra Eng): Rough calc: 1 GPU-month = $X (internal). 4 reserved vs 8 reserved is ~2x infra cost. Alternative: commit to 4 reserved + burst credits for occasional 4-GPU peaks; burst credits are cheaper for infrequent bursts. For their burst frequency (every 10 mins, 2m), cost favors reserved+burst credits, but SLA/latency guarantees better with fully reserved.
Mira (SE): For latency SLO <250ms at 95th, reserved+burst is OK if burst policy preallocates capacity within the same AZ and KV cache is warm. If cross-AZ cold-starts possible, prefer larger reserved pool.
Sara (Customer): Security Q: our compliance team needs local KMS integration and audit logs for inference. Is Private deploy required? Or can Dedicated with VPC peering satisfy?
Zach (Infra Eng): Dedicated with VPC peering + KMS integration (customer-managed keys) + audit log retention meets most controls. Private on-prem only if they require air-gapped or on-prem HSM.
Alex (Sales): Action items: 1) Mira to produce preheat script + warmup prompt set. 2) Zach to provide cost delta table (4 reserved vs 4+burst vs 8 reserved) and autoscale policy snippet. 3) Security doc snippet for KMS/logs. 4) Schedule dry-run preheat 48h before POC.
Mira (SE): I'll drop a warmup harness and sample load command. Example load command: 
```bash
load-gen --target-rps 600 --concurrency 300 --prompts-file warmup_prompts.json --duration 900
```
I'll also include the top-10 prompt list and their token lengths.
Zach (Infra Eng): Autoscale policy snippet: 
```yaml
min_gpus: 3
max_gpus: 8
scale_up: when(queue_depth > 40 && sustained > 30s)
scale_down: when(utilization < 30% for 120s)
burst_credits: enabled (reserve fallback)
```
I'll attach cost numbers in the follow-up.
Sara (Customer): Timeline OK. Also their procurement wants a single line item monthly commit if possible. Can you provide commit pricing vs overage?
Alex (Sales): I'll run commit vs burst pricing. Short answer: commit with 4 reserved + burst credits gives lowest expected cost with a predictable baseline invoice; overage mechanism for extreme peaks. I'll include explicit ARR math.
deploy-bot: Preheat job scheduled: job_id=preheat-175500-1, start=2025-09-10T14:00Z (subject to confirmation). :white_check_mark:
Mira (SE): One more thing — include KV cache TTLs in the preheat plan: set TTL >= 2h for POC window. That keeps cached prefixes across short bursts.
Zach (Infra Eng): Noted. I'll also add AZ affinity so burst capacity comes from same AZ to avoid cross-AZ cold starts.
Alex (Sales): Great. I'll send an updated SOW and the commit vs burst pricing by EOD. Sara — can you confirm procurement window and any extra compliance asks?
Sara (Customer): Procurement window is 2 weeks. Compliance: need SOC2 + KMS + audit retention 1 year. If you can provide those, we can sign commit.
Alex (Sales): Understood. Mir a/Zach — we'll include the compliance checklist in the SOW. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
